Economically, one of the results of the British rule in India in the 19th century was the (a) increase in the export of Indian handicrafts (b) growth in the number of Indian owned factories (c) commercialization of Indian agriculture (d) rapid increase in the urban population

questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). Commercialization of agriculture was the result of British rule in India in the 19th century. Farmers were forced to grow cash crops which were imported to Great Britain as raw materials of the English factories. The period also saw decline in urban population and destroyed domestic factories. Indians started producing crops for commercial use on a large scale. 19th-century agriculture became commercial due to the use of modern agricultural equipment. British rulers forced farmers to grow Indigo and other cash crops which can be used as a raw material for British manufactures. As a result urban population reduced and domestic Industries were destroyed. 49. Which of the following statements correctly explains the impact of Industrial Revolution on India during the ﬁ rst half of the nineteenth century? (a) Indian handicrafts were ruined. (b) Machines were introduced in the Indian textile industry in large numbers. (c) Railway lines were laid in many parts of the country. (d) Heavy duties were imposed on the imports of British manufacturers. I.A.S. (Pre) 2020 Ans (a) During the ﬁ rst half of 19th century, British policies have turned India as exporter of raw material and consumer of ﬁ nished product. Also because of Industrial Revolution in Britain, new machines were invented which were used to make handicraft products which were not just cheap but also of good quality which lead to downfall in demand of Indian handicraft products in domestic market too. Already they were unable to sell Indian goods at Britain because of high tariﬀ s. All this led to ruins of Indian handicrafts. Revolt of 1857 *In December 1856, the British Government decided to replace the old iron made Brown Bess (musket gun) with new and advanced Enﬁ eld Riﬂ e. Dum Dum, Ambala and Sialkot were decided the place for the trials of the new Gun. The Riﬂ e required the biting of the upper part of the cartridge by mouth. In January 1857, rumours spread that the cartridge contains fats of cow and pig. Army oﬃ cers without any investigation dismissed the rumours as fake news. But the soldiers believed this new Riﬂ e is an attempt to destroy their religions by the Britishers. It became the immediate reason for the Revolt of 1857. On 29 th March, 1857 soldiers of Barrakpore refused to use the fat-containing cartridges and, Mangal Pandey attacked and killed Sergeant Major's adjutant of his unit at Barrakpore. *Main reason of the Revolt of 1857 was the exploitative policies of Britishers and it was the outﬂ ow of all the dissents and grievances of Indians all of a sudden as an explosion in Volcano. *Anglo-Indian historians believed the Soldier’s discontentment and the fat-containing cartridges as the main and important reason for the Revolt of 1857. But modern historians proved this as only a reason followed by several other reasons. The fat-containing cartridges were just a spark which started the explosions of the explosives which were accumulated due to political, social, religious and economic discontents of Indians against the exploitative policies of British Rule. *Revolt of 1857 started on 10 th May, 1857 from Meerut where the 3 rd Bengal Light Cavalry regiment refused to touch the new cartridges and openly rebelled against the authorities. They ﬁ red on their oﬃ cers freed their inmates from cells and marched towards Delhi. Major General William Hewitt had 2200 European soldiers but he didn’t try to stop this storm. Revolters captured Delhi on 12 th May, 1857. Symbol of the 1857 revolt was Lotus and Chapatis (Bread). *Khan Bahadur, from Ruhelkhand, led the Revolt from Bareilly. He was appointed as the Viceroy by Mughal King Bahadur Shah II. *Rani Lakshmi Bai (Manikarnika) was born on 19 th November 1835 at Golghar (presently in Varanasi). At the age of 14 Laxmibai was married to Maharaja Gangadhar Rao who died in Gwalior. Rani Laxmi Bai was the widow of last Maratha king Gangadhar Rao. When Gangadhar Rao died without leaving any heir to the throne, Dalhousie by Doctrine of lapse, merged Jhansi to British Empire in 1854. *In June, 1857, the revolt began in Jhansi under the leadership of Rani Laxmi Bai. She died on 18 th June, 1858 ﬁ ghting General Hugh Henry Rose. On her death, Huge Rose said, “Among the Indian revolutionaries the women lying here is the only man.” *Revolt in Lucknow began under the leadership of Begam Hazrat Mahal on 30 th May, 1857. She declared her minor son Bijris Kadir as Nawab and took to all aﬀ airs of the Lucknow to herself. On 21 st March, 1858, Campbell with the help of Gurkha Regiment regained Lucknow. *On June 5 th 1857, Nana Shaheb (Nana Dhondho Pant) was declared Peshwa and the war of independence started in Kanpur. He was helped a lot by Commander-in-Chief Tatya Tope who was called as the Ambassador of Revolt. The original name of Tatya Tope was Ramchandra Pandurang. After being betrayed by a close friend Man Singh, he was captured when he was camping in a forest. From there he was brought to Shivpuri where a Court on 18 th April, 1859 sentenced him to be hanged till death. *Kunwar Singh led the revolt from Jagdishpur, Bihar. He was from Shahabad district (currently Bhojpur district) Bihar. *Deewan Maniram Dutt in Assam declared Kandpeshwar Singh the grandson of the last king as the king and started the revolt of 1857 there. But soon after Maniram Dutt was caught and hanged for the promotional activities of revolt. *Thakur Kushal Singh of Auwa defeated the combined army of English and Jodhpur. *Maulavi Ahmadullah Shah provided leadership to the revolt from Faizabad (Ayodhya) in 1857. He was a brutal enemy of Englishmen. He was native to Chinapattan of Madras, but he migrated to Faizabad. He asked all the diﬀ erent religious believers to stand as one against these English foreigners and to wipe them out from India. About him, Britishers said person ﬁ lled with extraordinary bravery and immovable, strong determination is the best soldier among all revolutionaries. A bounty of Rs. 50,000 for his arrest. *Mirza Ghalib saw the revolt of 1857 with his own eyes. He was born on 27 th December, 1797 in Agra and died in Delhi on 15 th February, 1869. *Shindhiyas of Gwalior helped the Britishers in the suppression of the Revolt.* Minister of Gwalior Sir Dinkar Rao was praised by European historians for his loyalty to English. Minister of Hyderabad Salar Jung was praised in the same way for his loyalty. *The revolt of 1857 was spread on a huge area and was fully supported by the public. But still, this Revolt was unable to bring whole of India together. This Revolt was unable to inﬂ uence the southern, western and eastern parts of India. *Shindhiya of Gwalior, Holker of Indore, Nizam of Hyderabad, King of Jodhpur, Nawab of Bhopal, Sikh rulers of Patiala, Nabha and Jind and other Sikh Sardar of Punjab, Maharaja of Kashmir and other kings were actively helping the Britishers in suppressing the revolts. To these rulers, Governor-General Canning said, : These rulers acted as barriers against the high and fast- moving wave of seas, in the absence of which we would have washed out from India completely. The Educated Class didn’t show any interest in the Revolt of 1857 which was one of the major cause of the failure of this Revolt. *Lord Canning (1856-62) was the Governor-General during the revolt of 1857. During the Revolt, he made Allahabad as an emergency headquarter. Lord Canning was the last Governor- General appointed by the Company and was the ﬁ rst Viceroy appointed by the British King. *Under the judicial reforms, Canning through Indian High Court Act established High Courts at Bombay, Calcutta and Madras. Under the social reforms Canning passed Hindu Widow Remarriage Act, 1856. The Sepoy Mutiny of 1857 is known as First War of Independence in India and as an Indian Mutiny in England. *Sir Syed Ahmed Khan wrote Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind which was published in 1859.* R.C Majumdar was appointed by Government of India to write on the Revolt of 1857, but due to diﬀ erences with the government committee he rejected this proposal, and he published his book “The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857” on his own in 1957. *R.C. Majumdar said, “ It is diﬃ cult to avoid the conclusion that the so-called First National War of Independence of 1857 is neither First, nor national, nor a war of Independence”. *Most important outcome of 1857 was the Queen’s Proclamation of 1858. It was declared on 1 st November, 1858 in Allahabad by Lord Canning ending the Company Rule and putting the Realm of British India under the direct control of Crown. This declaration included a ban on further British India expansion, no further interference in the religious matters of people, equal protection of law to be available to all. British stopped all further annexation of native states and kings were allowed to adopt. *After the Suppression of 1857 Revolt, ‘Peel Commission’ was constituted for the reorganization of Indian Army by British Government. The Commission divided the army on the basis of caste, religion, race, community, etc. The number of European soldiers was increased from 45,000 in 1857 to 65,000 by 1858. Indian troops were reduced from 2,38,000 to 1,40,000.The ratio of Europeans to Indian soldiers in Bengal was 1:2 whereas in Madras and Bombay it was 1:3. After the Revolt the soldiers were recruited more from Gorkha, Sikh and Punjab province. *John Bennet Hearsey was the commanding oﬃ cer of Barrakpore when Revolt of 1857 broke there. *Viscount Palmerston was the then Prime Minister of England. His tenure as Prime Minister was from 1855 to 1858 and 1859 to 1865. *The Revolt was poorly organized with no coordination or central leadership. The Mutineers lacked a clear understanding of Colonial Rule, nor did they have a forward- looking programme, a coherent ideology, a political perspective or societal alternatives. The Lack of unity among Indians proved detrimental for this Revolt. Modern Nationalism was not known to them at that time which led to everyone ﬁ ghting for their own interest and not for the nation. *Brigadier General John Nicholson died on 23 rd September, 1857 trying to recapture Delhi. Sir Henry Montgomery Lawrence, Major General Henry Havelock and Brigadier General Neil died in Lucknow in 1857 revolt protecting British Residency. Sir James Outram and W. Taylor termed the Revolt of 1857 as a result of a conspiracy of Hindu and Muslim.Outram said This was Muslim conspiracy in which the Hindu’s concerns were used for the Revolt. It was only a Sepoy Mutiny, according to John Lawrence and Seeley. According to T.R. Holmes, it was a war between Barbarism and Civilization. V. D. Savarkar in his book “The Indian war of Independence 1857”, termed this Revolt as an organized struggle for Independence. He said it was the First War of Independence. *The Government Historian on Indian independence movement was Surendra Nath Sen whose book ‘Eighteen Fifty-Seven’ was published in 1957. 1. When was the new Enﬁ eld Riﬂ e with greased cartridges introduced in the British Indian Army? (a) November, 1856 (b) December, 1856 (c) January, 1857 (d) February, 1857 47th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2005 Ans. (b) The Company decided to use new Enﬁ eld Riﬂ e instead of old Brown Bess gun in December, 1856. The training for the use of this riﬂ e was organized in Dum Dum, Ambala, and Sialkot. The riﬂ e needed an extraordinary kind of loading of a cartridge in the magazine and hence the soldiers while in the ensuing ﬁ ght, had to bite oﬀ the outer covering of the cartridge while loading it down into the riﬂ e’s muzzle. The cartridge was rumoured to have been greased with animal fat (Pig fat and Cow fat). Army Commanders refused rumours without any cross-checking, but the soldiers were of the view that this was an intentional act of the British to besmirch their religion. This became the immediate cause ﬁ rst Independence Struggle of India in 1857. 2. The immediate cause of India’s ﬁ rst war of independence was: (a) Doctrine of Lapse by Lord Dalhousie (b) Suspicion about British interference in religion (c) Military discontent (d) Economic exploitation of India R.A.S./R.T.S. (Pre) 1993 Ans. (b) See the explanation of the above question. 3. Mangal Pandey incident took place at: (a) Meerut (b) Barrackpore (c) Ambala (d) Lucknow Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Mains) 2002 Ans. (b) Soldiers denied to use a cartridge of animal fat in Barrackpore 29 March, 1857 and Mangal Pandey murdered his Sergeant Major's adjutant. British dissolved 34th Bengal Native Infantry Regiment and punished the culprits.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (C) कृषि का व्यावसायीकरण 19वीं शताब्दी में भारत में ब्रिटिश शासन का परिणाम था। किसानों को नकदी फसलें उगाने के लिए मजबूर किया गया जिन्हें अंग्रेजी कारखानों के कच्चे माल के रूप में ग्रेट ब्रिटेन में आयात किया गया था। इस अवधि में शहरी आबादी में भी गिरावट देखी गई और घरेलू कारखाने नष्ट हो गए। भारतीयों ने बड़े पैमाने पर व्यावसायिक उपयोग के लिए फसलें पैदा करना शुरू कर दिया। आधुनिक कृषि उपकरणों के उपयोग के कारण 19वीं सदी की कृषि व्यावसायिक हो गई। ब्रिटिश शासकों ने किसानों को नील और अन्य नकदी फसलें उगाने के लिए मजबूर किया, जिनका उपयोग ब्रिटिश निर्माताओं के लिए कच्चे माल के रूप में किया जा सकता है। परिणामस्वरूप शहरी जनसंख्या कम हो गई और घरेलू उद्योग नष्ट हो गए। 49. निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन उन्नीसवीं शताब्दी के पूर्वार्द्ध के दौरान भारत पर औद्योगिक क्रांति के प्रभाव की सही व्याख्या करता है? (ए) भारतीय हस्तशिल्प बर्बाद हो गए। (बी) भारतीय कपड़ा उद्योग में बड़ी संख्या में मशीनें पेश की गईं। (सी) देश के कई हिस्सों में रेलवे लाइनें बिछाई गईं। (डी) ब्रिटिश निर्माताओं के आयात पर भारी शुल्क लगाया गया। आई.ए.एस. (पूर्व) 2020 उत्तर (ए) 19वीं शताब्दी के पूर्वार्द्ध के दौरान, ब्रिटिश नीतियों ने भारत को कच्चे माल के निर्यातक और तैयार उत्पाद के उपभोक्ता के रूप में बदल दिया है। इसके अलावा ब्रिटेन में औद्योगिक क्रांति के कारण, नई मशीनों का आविष्कार हुआ जिनका उपयोग हस्तशिल्प उत्पाद बनाने के लिए किया गया जो न केवल सस्ते थे बल्कि अच्छी गुणवत्ता वाले भी थे जिसके कारण घरेलू बाजार में भी भारतीय हस्तशिल्प उत्पादों की मांग में गिरावट आई। पहले से ही वे उच्च टैरिफ के कारण ब्रिटेन में भारतीय सामान बेचने में असमर्थ थे। यह सब भारतीय हस्तशिल्प के खंडहर का कारण बना। 1857 का विद्रोह *दिसंबर 1856 में, ब्रिटिश सरकार ने पुरानी लोहे से बनी ब्राउन बेस (मस्कट गन) को नई और उन्नत एनफील्ड राइफल से बदलने का फैसला किया। नई तोप के परीक्षण के लिए दमदम, अंबाला और सियालकोट को स्थान तय किया गया। राइफल को मुंह से कारतूस के ऊपरी हिस्से को काटने की आवश्यकता होती थी। जनवरी 1857 में अफवाह फैल गई कि कारतूस में गाय और सुअर की चर्बी है। सेना के अधिकारियों ने बिना किसी जांच के अफवाहों को फर्जी खबर बताकर खारिज कर दिया। लेकिन सैनिकों का मानना ​​था कि यह नई राइफल अंग्रेजों द्वारा उनके धर्मों को नष्ट करने का एक प्रयास है। यह 1857 के विद्रोह का तात्कालिक कारण बन गया। 29 मार्च, 1857 को बैरकपुर के सैनिकों ने वसा युक्त कारतूसों का उपयोग करने से इनकार कर दिया और, मंगल पांडे ने बैरकपुर में अपनी इकाई के सार्जेंट मेजर के सहायक पर हमला किया और उसकी हत्या कर दी। *1857 के विद्रोह का मुख्य कारण अंग्रेजों की शोषणकारी नीतियां थीं और यह ज्वालामुखी में विस्फोट के रूप में भारतीयों की सभी असहमतियों और शिकायतों का अचानक समाधान था। *एंग्लो-इंडियन इतिहासकारों ने सैनिकों के असंतोष और चर्बी युक्त कारतूसों को 1857 के विद्रोह का मुख्य और महत्वपूर्ण कारण माना। लेकिन आधुनिक इतिहासकारों ने इसे केवल एक कारण साबित किया और इसके बाद कई अन्य कारण भी बताए। चर्बी युक्त कारतूस महज एक चिंगारी थी जिसने ब्रिटिश शासन की शोषणकारी नीतियों के खिलाफ भारतीयों के राजनीतिक, सामाजिक, धार्मिक और आर्थिक असंतोष के कारण जमा हुए विस्फोटकों के विस्फोट शुरू कर दिए। *1857 का विद्रोह 10 मई, 1857 को मेरठ से शुरू हुआ, जहां तीसरी बंगाल लाइट कैवेलरी रेजिमेंट ने नए कारतूसों को छूने से इनकार कर दिया और अधिकारियों के खिलाफ खुले तौर पर विद्रोह कर दिया। उन्होंने अपने अधिकारियों पर हमला बोलकर अपने कैदियों को कोठरियों से मुक्त कर दिया और दिल्ली की ओर कूच कर दिया। मेजर जनरल विलियम हेविट के पास 2200 यूरोपीय सैनिक थे लेकिन उन्होंने इस तूफ़ान को रोकने की कोशिश नहीं की. 12 मई, 1857 को विद्रोहियों ने दिल्ली पर कब्ज़ा कर लिया। 1857 के विद्रोह का प्रतीक कमल और चपाती था। *रुहेलखंड के खान बहादुर ने बरेली से विद्रोह का नेतृत्व किया। उन्हें मुगल राजा बहादुर शाह द्वितीय द्वारा वायसराय के रूप में नियुक्त किया गया था। *रानी लक्ष्मी बाई (मणिकर्णिका) का जन्म 19 नवंबर 1835 को गोलघर (वर्तमान में वाराणसी) में हुआ था। 14 साल की उम्र में लक्ष्मीबाई का विवाह महाराजा गंगाधर राव से हुआ जिनकी मृत्यु ग्वालियर में हुई। रानी लक्ष्मी बाई अंतिम मराठा राजा गंगाधर राव की विधवा थीं। जब के मंत्री सालार जंग की वफादारी के लिए इसी तरह तारीफ की गई. *1857 का विद्रोह बहुत बड़े क्षेत्र में फैला हुआ था और इसे जनता का पूरा समर्थन प्राप्त था। परन्तु फिर भी यह विद्रोह सम्पूर्ण भारत को एक साथ कहा, : इन शासकों ने समुद्र की ऊंची और तेज गति से चलने वाली लहरों के खिलाफ बाधाओं के रूप में काम किया, जिनके अभाव में हम भारत से पूरी तरह से बह गए होते। शिक्षित वर्ग ने 1857 के विद्रोह में कोई रुचि कंपनी द्वारा नियुक्त अंतिम गवर्नर-जनरल थे और ब्रिटिश राजा द्वारा नियुक्त पहले वायसराय थे। *न्यायिक सुधारों के तहत, कैनिंग ने भारतीय उच्च न्यायालय अधिनियम के माध्यम से बॉम्बे, कलकत्ता और मद्रास में इलाहाबाद में लॉर्ड कैनिंग द्वारा कंपनी शासन को समाप्त करने और ब्रिटिश भारत के क्षेत्र को क्राउन के सीधे नियंत्रण में रखने की घोषणा की गई थी। इस घोषणा में ब्रिटिश भारत के आगे विस्तार पर प्रतिबंध, लोगों Revolt of 1857 *In December 1856, the British Government decided to replace the old iron made Brown Bess (musket gun) with new and advanced Enﬁ eld Riﬂ e. Dum Dum, Ambala and Sialkot were decided the place for the trials of the new Gun. The Riﬂ e required the biting of the upper part of the cartridge by mouth. In January 1857, rumours spread that the cartridge contains fats of cow and pig. Army oﬃ cers without any investigation dismissed the rumours as fake news. But the soldiers believed this new Riﬂ e is an attempt to destroy their religions by the Britishers. It became the immediate reason for the Revolt of 1857. On 29 th March, 1857 soldiers of Barrakpore refused to use the fat-containing cartridges and, Mangal Pandey attacked and killed Sergeant Major's adjutant of his unit at Barrakpore. *Main reason of the Revolt of 1857 was the exploitative policies of Britishers and it was the outﬂ ow of all the dissents and grievances of Indians all of a sudden as an explosion in Volcano. *Anglo-Indian historians believed the Soldier’s discontentment and the fat-containing cartridges as the main and important reason for the Revolt of 1857. But modern historians proved this as only a reason followed by several other reasons. The fat-containing cartridges were just a spark which started the explosions of the explosives which were accumulated due to political, social, religious and economic discontents of Indians against the exploitative policies of British Rule. *Revolt of 1857 started on 10 th May, 1857 from Meerut where the 3 rd Bengal Light Cavalry regiment refused to touch the new cartridges and openly rebelled against the authorities. They ﬁ red on their oﬃ cers freed their inmates from cells and marched towards Delhi. Major General William Hewitt had 2200 European soldiers but he didn’t try to stop this storm. Revolters captured Delhi on 12 th May, 1857. Symbol of the 1857 revolt was Lotus and Chapatis (Bread). *Khan Bahadur, from Ruhelkhand, led the Revolt from Bareilly. He was appointed as the Viceroy by Mughal King Bahadur Shah II. *Rani Lakshmi Bai (Manikarnika) was born on 19 th November 1835 at Golghar (presently in Varanasi). At the age of 14 Laxmibai was married to Maharaja Gangadhar Rao who died in Gwalior. Rani Laxmi Bai was the widow of last Maratha king Gangadhar Rao. When Gangadhar Rao died without leaving any heir to the throne, Dalhousie by Doctrine of lapse, merged Jhansi to British Empire in 1854. *In June, 1857, the revolt began in Jhansi under the leadership of Rani Laxmi Bai. She died on 18 th June, 1858 ﬁ ghting General Hugh Henry Rose. On her death, Huge Rose said, “Among the Indian revolutionaries the women lying here is the only man.” *Revolt in Lucknow began under the leadership of Begam Hazrat Mahal on 30 th May, 1857. She declared her minor son Bijris Kadir as Nawab and took to all aﬀ airs of the Lucknow to herself. On 21 st March, 1858, Campbell with the help of Gurkha Regiment regained Lucknow. *On June 5 th 1857, Nana Shaheb (Nana Dhondho Pant) was declared Peshwa and the war of independence started in Kanpur. He was helped a lot by Commander-in-Chief Tatya Tope who was called as the Ambassador of Revolt. The original name of Tatya Tope was Ramchandra Pandurang. After being betrayed by a close friend Man Singh, he was captured when he was camping in a forest. From there he was brought to Shivpuri where a Court on 18 th April, 1859 sentenced him to be hanged till death. *Kunwar Singh led the revolt from Jagdishpur, Bihar. He was from Shahabad district (currently Bhojpur district) Bihar. *Deewan Maniram Dutt in Assam declared Kandpeshwar Singh the grandson of the last king as the king and started the revolt of 1857 there. But soon after Maniram Dutt was caught and hanged for the promotional activities of revolt. *Thakur Kushal Singh of Auwa defeated the combined army of English and Jodhpur. *Maulavi Ahmadullah Shah provided leadership to the revolt from Faizabad (Ayodhya) in 1857. He was a brutal enemy of Englishmen. He was native to Chinapattan of Madras, but he migrated to Faizabad. He asked all the diﬀ erent religious believers to stand as one against these English foreigners and to wipe them out from India. About him, Britishers said person ﬁ lled with extraordinary bravery and immovable, strong determination is the best soldier among all revolutionaries. A bounty of Rs. 50,000 for his arrest. *Mirza Ghalib saw the revolt of 1857 with his own eyes. He was born on 27 th December, 1797 in Agra and died in Delhi on 15 th February, 1869. *Shindhiyas of Gwalior helped the Britishers in the suppression of the Revolt.* Minister of Gwalior Sir Dinkar Rao was praised by European historians for his loyalty to English. Minister of Hyderabad Salar Jung was praised in the same way for his loyalty. *The revolt of 1857 was spread on a huge area and was fully supported by the public. But still, this Revolt was unable to bring whole of India together. This Revolt was unable to inﬂ uence the southern, western and eastern parts of India. *Shindhiya of Gwalior, Holker of Indore, Nizam of Hyderabad, King of Jodhpur, Nawab of Bhopal, Sikh rulers of Patiala, Nabha and Jind and other Sikh Sardar of Punjab, Maharaja of Kashmir and other kings were actively helping the Britishers in suppressing the revolts. To these rulers, Governor-General Canning said, : These rulers acted as barriers against the high and fast- moving wave of seas, in the absence of which we would have washed out from India completely. The Educated Class didn’t show any interest in the Revolt of 1857 which was one of the major cause of the failure of this Revolt. *Lord Canning (1856-62) was the Governor-General during the revolt of 1857. During the Revolt, he made Allahabad as an emergency headquarter. Lord Canning was the last Governor- General appointed by the Company and was the ﬁ rst Viceroy appointed by the British King. *Under the judicial reforms, Canning through Indian High Court Act established High Courts at Bombay, Calcutta and Madras. Under the social reforms Canning passed Hindu Widow Remarriage Act, 1856. The Sepoy Mutiny of 1857 is known as First War of Independence in India and as an Indian Mutiny in England. *Sir Syed Ahmed Khan wrote Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind which was published in 1859.* R.C Majumdar was appointed by Government of India to write on the Revolt of 1857, but due to diﬀ erences with the government committee he rejected this proposal, and he published his book “The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857” on his own in 1957. *R.C. Majumdar said, “ It is diﬃ cult to avoid the conclusion that the so-called First National War of Independence of 1857 is neither First, nor national, nor a war of Independence”. *Most important outcome of 1857 was the Queen’s Proclamation of 1858. It was declared on 1 st November, 1858 in Allahabad by Lord Canning ending the Company Rule and putting the Realm of British India under the direct control of Crown. This declaration included a ban on further British India expansion, no further interference in the religious matters of people, equal protection of law to be available to all. British stopped all further annexation of native states and kings were allowed to adopt. *After the Suppression of 1857 Revolt, ‘Peel Commission’ was constituted for the reorganization of Indian Army by British Government. The Commission divided the army on the basis of caste, religion, race, community, etc. The number of European soldiers was increased from 45,000 in 1857 to 65,000 by 1858. Indian troops were reduced from 2,38,000 to 1,40,000.The ratio of Europeans to Indian soldiers in Bengal was 1:2 whereas in Madras and Bombay it was 1:3. After the Revolt the soldiers were recruited more from Gorkha, Sikh and Punjab province. *John Bennet Hearsey was the commanding oﬃ cer of Barrakpore when Revolt of 1857 broke there. *Viscount Palmerston was the then Prime Minister of England. His tenure as Prime Minister was from 1855 to 1858 and 1859 to 1865. *The Revolt was poorly organized with no coordination or central leadership. The Mutineers lacked a clear understanding of Colonial Rule, nor did they have a forward- looking programme, a coherent ideology, a political perspective or societal alternatives. The Lack of unity among Indians proved detrimental for this Revolt. Modern Nationalism was not known to them at that time which led to everyone ﬁ ghting for their own interest and not for the nation. *Brigadier General John Nicholson died on 23 rd September, 1857 trying to recapture Delhi. Sir Henry Montgomery Lawrence, Major General Henry Havelock and Brigadier General Neil died in Lucknow in 1857 revolt protecting British Residency. Sir James Outram and W. Taylor termed the Revolt of 1857 as a result of a conspiracy of Hindu and Muslim.Outram said This was Muslim conspiracy in which the Hindu’s concerns were used for the Revolt. It was only a Sepoy Mutiny, according to John Lawrence and Seeley. According to T.R. Holmes, it was a war between Barbarism and Civilization. V. D. Savarkar in his book “The Indian war of Independence 1857”, termed this Revolt as an organized struggle for Independence. He said it was the First War of Independence. *The Government Historian on Indian independence movement was Surendra Nath Sen whose book ‘Eighteen Fifty-Seven’ was published in 1957. 1. questions.questionTextEn: What was the main cause of 1857 revolt?
questions.questionTextHi: 1857 के विद्रोह का मुख्य कारण क्या था?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). The Indian Rebellion of 1857 had diverse political, economic, military, religious and social causes. The sepoys, a generic term used for native Indian soldiers of the Bengal Army, had their own list of grievances against the British East India Company administration. The spark that led to the mutiny was the issue of new gunpowder cartridges for Enﬁ eld riﬂ e in January 1857. There was a widespread belief that the cartridges contained cow or pig fat. This insulted both the Hindu and Muslim religious practices. Underlying grievances like taxation and land annexations by East India company were ignited by the sepoy mutineers, and within weeks dozens of units of Indian army joined the peasant army in widespread rebellion. The old aristocracy, both Muslim and Hindu, who were seeing their power being steadily eroded by the East India company also rebelled against British rule.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (D) 1857 के भारतीय विद्रोह के विविध राजनीतिक, आर्थिक, सैन्य, धार्मिक और सामाजिक कारण थे। सिपाही, जो बंगाल सेना के मूल भारतीय सैनिकों के लिए इस्तेमाल किया जाने वाला एक सामान्य शब्द है, की ब्रिटिश ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी प्रशासन के खिलाफ शिकायतों की अपनी सूची थी। विद्रोह की चिंगारी जनवरी 1857 में एनफील्ड राइफल के लिए नए बारूद कारतूसों का मुद्दा था। व्यापक धारणा थी कि कारतूसों में गाय या सुअर की चर्बी होती थी। इससे हिंदू और मुस्लिम दोनों की धार्मिक प्रथाओं का अपमान हुआ। ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी द्वारा कराधान और भूमि अधिग्रहण जैसी अंतर्निहित शिकायतों को सिपाही विद्रोहियों ने भड़का दिया, और कुछ ही हफ्तों में भारतीय सेना की दर्जनों इकाइयाँ व्यापक विद्रोह में किसान सेना में शामिल हो गईं। पुराने अभिजात वर्ग, मुस्लिम और हिंदू दोनों, जो ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी द्वारा अपनी शक्ति को लगातार कम होते देख रहे थे, उन्होंने भी ब्रिटिश शासन के खिलाफ विद्रोह कर दिया।

questions.questionTextEn: The ﬁ rst war of Independence (1857) started from:
questions.questionTextHi: प्रथम स्वतंत्रता संग्राम (1857) कहाँ से प्रारंभ हुआ?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). The ﬁ rst war of Independence was started from Meerut. Sepoys refused to use the new riﬂ e cartridges and revolted openly. They left Meerut and moved to Delhi. Major General William Hewitt had not tried to stop this rebellion. Lieutenant General George Dobson Precival Willoughby resisted, but he was defeated. Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar was declared Emperor of India. The success of Delhi revolt sensitized many parts of India and revolt spread over to the areas of Oudh, Rohillkhand, Western Bihar, etc.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (C) प्रथम स्वतंत्रता संग्राम की शुरुआत मेरठ से हुई थी। सिपाहियों ने नई राइफल कारतूसों का उपयोग करने से इनकार कर दिया और खुलेआम विद्रोह कर दिया। वे मेरठ छोड़कर दिल्ली चले गये। मेजर जनरल विलियम हेविट ने इस विद्रोह को रोकने का प्रयास नहीं किया था। लेफ्टिनेंट जनरल जॉर्ज डॉब्सन प्रीसिवल विलॉबी ने विरोध किया, लेकिन वह हार गए। मुगल सम्राट बहादुर शाह जफर को भारत का सम्राट घोषित किया गया। दिल्ली विद्रोह की सफलता ने भारत के कई हिस्सों को संवेदनशील बना दिया और विद्रोह अवध, रोहिलखंड, पश्चिमी बिहार आदि क्षेत्रों में फैल गया।

optionsEn: The eﬀ orts of the oﬃ cers of the company to spread Christianity
The order to the sepoys to travel on ships
The ineﬃ ciency of the oﬃ cers (e) None of the above/More than one of the above

सिपाहियों को जहाज़ों पर यात्रा करने का आदेश
अधिकारियों की अक्षमता (ई) उपरोक्त में से कोई नहीं/उपरोक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). The ineﬃ ciency of the oﬃ cers was not a cause for the Sepoy Mutiny. The Indian Rebellion of 1857 occurred as a result of an accumulation of factors over time, rather than any single event, like an eﬀ ort by oﬃ cers to spread Christianity among the soldiers led to interference in the religious matters of the people. The order of the Company to the sepoys to travel on a ship was another reason as in Hinduism it was believed that travelling by sea could deprive them of their religious status of being a Hindu. A more immediate cause of the sepoy’s dissatisfaction was the recent order that they would not be given the foreign service allowance (Bhatta/Batta) when serving in Sindh or Punjab and rumours of the use of animal fat in the cartridges of the New Enﬁ eld Riﬂ e.

questions.questionTextEn: The symbol of 1857 independence struggle was –
questions.questionTextHi: 1857 के स्वतंत्रता संग्राम का प्रतीक चिन्ह था -
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). The symbol of 1857 Independence struggle were Chapatis (bread) and Lotus. A class of historians considers that this mutiny was a wide and well-planned conspiracy. They mentioned the reach of Chapatis and Lotus in remote villages of North India and prophets, hermit and plays of Madaris to prove that fact.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (A) 1857 के स्वतंत्रता संग्राम का प्रतीक चपातियाँ और कमल थे। इतिहासकारों का एक वर्ग मानता है कि यह विद्रोह एक व्यापक एवं सुनियोजित षड़यंत्र था। उन्होंने इस तथ्य को सिद्ध करने के लिए उत्तर भारत के सुदूर गाँवों में चपाती और कमल की पहुँच तथा पैगम्बरों, साधुओं और मदारियों के नाटकों का उल्लेख किया।

questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following centres of the uprising of 1857 was recaptured by the English?
questions.questionTextHi: 1857 के विद्रोह के निम्नलिखित केंद्रों में से किस पर अंग्रेज़ों ने पुनः कब्ज़ा कर लिया था?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). The ﬁ rst expression of organized resistance was the Revolt of 1857. It began as a revolt of the Sepoys of the Company’s army but eventually secured the participation of the masses. The Meerut Mutiny marked the beginning of the Revolt of 1857. The Indian sepoys in Meerut murdered their British oﬃ cers and broke the jail. On May 10, they marched to Delhi. In Delhi, the mutineers were joined by the Delhi sepoys, and the city came under their control. Next day, on 11th May, the sepoys proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar as the Emperor of Hindustan. But Bahadur Shah was old, and he could not give able leadership to the sepoys. The occupation of Delhi was short-lived. In May 1857 the Battle of Shamli took place between the forces of Hazi Imdadullah and the British. The Sikhs and Pathans of the Punjab and North-West Frontier Province supported the British and helped to recapture Delhi on 20th September, 1857.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (C) संगठित प्रतिरोध की पहली अभिव्यक्ति 1857 का विद्रोह था। यह कंपनी की सेना के सिपाहियों के विद्रोह के रूप में शुरू हुआ लेकिन अंततः जनता की भागीदारी सुनिश्चित हुई। मेरठ विद्रोह ने 1857 के विद्रोह की शुरुआत को चिह्नित किया। मेरठ में भारतीय सिपाहियों ने अपने ब्रिटिश अधिकारियों की हत्या कर दी और जेल तोड़ दी। 10 मई को उन्होंने दिल्ली तक मार्च किया. दिल्ली में, विद्रोहियों में दिल्ली के सिपाही भी शामिल हो गए और शहर उनके नियंत्रण में आ गया। अगले दिन 11 मई को सिपाहियों ने बहादुर शाह जफर को हिंदुस्तान का बादशाह घोषित कर दिया। लेकिन बहादुर शाह बूढ़ा हो गया था और वह सिपाहियों को सक्षम नेतृत्व नहीं दे सका। दिल्ली पर कब्ज़ा अल्पकालिक था। मई 1857 में शामली की लड़ाई हाजी इमदादुल्लाह की सेना और अंग्रेजों के बीच हुई। पंजाब और उत्तर-पश्चिम सीमा प्रांत के सिखों और पठानों ने अंग्रेजों का समर्थन किया और 20 सितंबर, 1857 को दिल्ली पर दोबारा कब्ज़ा करने में मदद की।

questions.questionTextEn: The birthplace of Maharani Laxmi Bai, the heroine of the 1857 freedom struggle, is:
questions.questionTextHi: 1857 के स्वतंत्रता संग्राम की वीरांगना महारानी लक्ष्मीबाई का जन्मस्थान है:
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). Rani Laxmibai, originally known as Manikarnika, was born on 19 November, 1835 in Golghar, Varanasi. His father Moropant went to the court of King Gangadhar Rao. She was married to Maharaja Gangadhar Rao of Jhansi at the age of 14.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (C) रानी लक्ष्मीबाई, जिन्हें मूल रूप से मणिकर्णिका के नाम से जाना जाता था, का जन्म 19 नवंबर, 1835 को गोलघर, वाराणसी में हुआ था। उनके पिता मोरोपंत राजा गंगाधर राव के दरबार में गये। 14 साल की उम्र में उनका विवाह झाँसी के महाराजा गंगाधर राव से हुआ।

questions.questionTextEn: Who among the following was the leader of the revolt during 1857 at Bareilly?
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन 1857 के दौरान बरेली में विद्रोह का नेता था?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). Khan Bahadur led the revolt of 1857 in Bareilly. He organized an army of 40 thousand soldiers and battled hard with Britishers. Bahadur Shah II appointed him Viceroy. He treated Hindus and Muslims equally and reﬂ ected his able administration.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (A) खान बहादुर ने बरेली में 1857 के विद्रोह का नेतृत्व किया। उन्होंने 40 हजार सैनिकों की एक सेना संगठित की और अंग्रेजों से कड़ा संघर्ष किया। बहादुर शाह द्वितीय ने उन्हें वायसराय नियुक्त किया। उन्होंने हिंदुओं और मुसलमानों के साथ समान व्यवहार किया और अपने कुशल प्रशासन का परिचय दिया।

questions.questionTextHi: महारानी लक्ष्मीबाई ने अंतिम युद्ध किसके विरुद्ध लड़ा था?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). Rani Laxmibai was the widow of the last Jhansi king Raja Gangadhar Rao. Dalhousie annexed Jhansi with his ‘Doctrine of Lapse’ in 1854. The revolt started under the leadership of Rani Laxmibai in June, 1857. Rani departed for Gwalior after the decline of Jhansi. She achieved Martyrdom on 18 June, 1858 after a long battle. Hugh Rose said on the death of Rani “Sleeping Beauty is the only man among all Indian rebel leaders”.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (A) रानी लक्ष्मीबाई आखिरी झाँसी राजा राजा गंगाधर राव की विधवा थीं। डलहौजी ने 1854 में अपने 'डॉक्ट्रिन ऑफ लैप्स' के साथ झाँसी पर कब्ज़ा कर लिया। जून, 1857 में रानी लक्ष्मीबाई के नेतृत्व में विद्रोह शुरू हुआ। झाँसी के पतन के बाद रानी ग्वालियर के लिए प्रस्थान कर गईं। लंबी लड़ाई के बाद 18 जून, 1858 को उन्होंने शहादत प्राप्त की। ह्यू रोज़ ने रानी की मृत्यु पर कहा, "स्लीपिंग ब्यूटी सभी भारतीय विद्रोही नेताओं में एकमात्र पुरुष है"।

questions.questionTextHi: लखनऊ में 1857 के विद्रोह का नेतृत्व किया गया था:
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). The revolt was started on 30 May, 1857 in Oudh (Lucknow). The mutiny was led by Begum Hazrat Mahal. She crowned her minor son Birjis Qadir as royal heir and took charge of the aﬀ airs of the state of Oudh. Later, Colin Campbell reannexed Lucknow with the help of the Gorkha regiment on 21 March, 1858.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (A) विद्रोह की शुरुआत 30 मई, 1857 को अवध (लखनऊ) में हुई थी। विद्रोह का नेतृत्व बेगम हजरत महल ने किया था। उन्होंने अपने नाबालिग बेटे बिरजिस कादिर को शाही उत्तराधिकारी के रूप में ताज पहनाया और अवध राज्य के कामकाज की जिम्मेदारी संभाली। बाद में, कॉलिन कैंपबेल ने 21 मार्च, 1858 को गोरखा रेजिमेंट की मदद से लखनऊ पर दोबारा कब्ज़ा कर लिया।

questions.questionTextEn: Who amongst the following was the leader of the 1857 uprising at Allahabad?
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन इलाहाबाद में 1857 के विद्रोह का नेता था?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). Maulvi Liyaqat Ali was a Muslim religious leader from Allahabad (Prayagraj), in Uttar Pradesh. He was one of the leaders of the revolt against the British in 1857. One of the most prominent leaders of the 1857 Sepoy Mutiny, Maulvi Liyaqat Ali belonged to Village Mahgaon in Chail Pargana of District Allahabad (Prayagraj). He was a religious teacher, an upright, pious Muslim and a man of great courage and bravery. Maulvi captured Khusro Bagh and declared the Independence of India. Khusro Bagh became the headquarters of the sepoys under Maulvi Liyaqat Ali who took charge as the Governor of liberated Allahabad. Later this mutiny was suppressed by General Neil.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (D) मौलवी लियाकत अली उत्तर प्रदेश के इलाहाबाद (प्रयागराज) के एक मुस्लिम धार्मिक नेता थे। वह 1857 में अंग्रेजों के खिलाफ विद्रोह के नेताओं में से एक थे। 1857 के सिपाही विद्रोह के सबसे प्रमुख नेताओं में से एक, मौलवी लियाकत अली जिला इलाहाबाद (प्रयागराज) के चैल परगना के ग्राम महगांव के थे। वह एक धार्मिक शिक्षक, एक ईमानदार, धर्मपरायण मुसलमान और महान साहस और बहादुरी के व्यक्ति थे। मौलवी ने खुसरो बाग पर कब्ज़ा कर लिया और भारत की आज़ादी की घोषणा कर दी। खुसरो बाग मौलवी लियाकत अली के अधीन सिपाहियों का मुख्यालय बन गया, जिन्होंने आज़ाद इलाहाबाद के राज्यपाल के रूप में कार्यभार संभाला। बाद में इस विद्रोह को जनरल नील ने दबा दिया।

questions.questionTextEn: With reference to the ‘revolt of 1857’ who of the following was betrayed by ‘friend’ captured and put to death by the British?
questions.questionTextHi: '1857 के विद्रोह' के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से किसको 'मित्र' ने धोखा दिया था जिसे अंग्रेजों ने पकड़ लिया और मौत की सजा दे दी?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). Ramachandra Pandurang, known as Tatya Tope, was an able leader of the great uprising of 1857. He was a personal adherent of Nana Saheb of Kanpur. He progressed with the Gwalior contingent after the British reoccupation of Kanpur and forced Lieutenant General Charles Ash Windham to retreat from Kanpur. Later on, he came to the rescue of Rani Laxmi Bai. However, he was defeated by General Napier‘s troops and was executed by the British Government (after he was captured in the forest of paron due to betrayal of his friend Mansingh) at Shivpuri on 18th April 1859. One of the greatest heroes of the Great Uprising of 1857, Tatya Tope was born in 1814 at Yeola in Maharashtra. He was the only child of Pandurang and his wife, Rukhmabai. Having been brought up in Bithoor, he came into contact with Nana Saheb Peshwa. He was a great admirer of Nana Saheb and was ready to sacriﬁ ce his life for him. Tatya Tope was the only person who witnessed the rebellion since the Kanpur revolt unitl his end on 18th April 1859.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (D) तात्या टोपे के नाम से जाने जाने वाले रामचन्द्र पांडुरंग 1857 के महान विद्रोह के एक सक्षम नेता थे। वह कानपुर के नाना साहब के निजी अनुयायी थे। अंग्रेजों द्वारा कानपुर पर पुनः कब्ज़ा करने के बाद वह ग्वालियर की टुकड़ी के साथ आगे बढ़े और लेफ्टिनेंट जनरल चार्ल्स ऐश विंडहैम को कानपुर से पीछे हटने के लिए मजबूर कर दिया। बाद में, वह रानी लक्ष्मीबाई के बचाव में आये। हालाँकि, वह जनरल नेपियर के सैनिकों से हार गए और 18 अप्रैल 1859 को शिवपुरी में ब्रिटिश सरकार द्वारा (अपने मित्र मानसिंह के विश्वासघात के कारण पारोन के जंगल में पकड़े जाने के बाद) उन्हें मार डाला गया। 1857 के महान विद्रोह के महानतम नायकों में से एक, तात्या टोपे का जन्म 1814 में महाराष्ट्र के येओला में हुआ था। वह पांडुरंग और उनकी पत्नी रुखमाबाई की एकमात्र संतान थे। बिठूर में पले बढ़े होने के कारण वे नाना साहब पेशवा के संपर्क में आये। वह नाना साहब के बहुत बड़े प्रशंसक थे और उनके लिए अपना जीवन बलिदान करने को तैयार थे। 18 अप्रैल 1859 को कानपुर विद्रोह इकाई के अंत के बाद से तात्या टोपे एकमात्र व्यक्ति थे जिन्होंने विद्रोह को देखा था।

questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following places did Kunwar Singh, a prominent leader of the Revolt of 1857 belong to?
questions.questionTextHi: 1857 के विद्रोह के प्रमुख नेता कुँवर सिंह निम्नलिखित में से किस स्थान से सम्बंधित थे?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). Kunwar Singh was one of the most important freedom ﬁ ghters in the Sepoy Mutiny of 1857. Kunwar Singh was born in Jagdishpur in Shahabad (now in Bhojpur District) of Bihar. He belonged to Arrah in Bihar during the mutiny. When the people of all parts of India rose against British authority in 1857, Babu Kunwar Singh was nearly eighty years old. At that age, he fought against the English East India Company. Despite his age and failing health, Kunwar Singh plunged into the thick of it and battled against the British forces with grim determination and undaunted courage. In Bihar, Kunwar Singh was the Leader against the British. He assumed command of the soldiers who had revolted at Danapur on 25th July 1857. Two days later he occupied Arrah, the district headquarters. Major Vincent Eyre relieved the town in August 1857, defeated Kunwar Singh’s force and destroyed Jagdishpur. Kunwar Singh left his ancestral village and reached Lucknow in December 1857. In March 1858, he occupied Azamgarh. However, he had to leave the place soon. He was pursued by Brigadier Douglas, and he retreated towards his home in Bihar. On 23 April 1858, Kunwar Singh had a victory near Jagdishpur over the force led by Captain Le Grand, but on 26 April 1858, he died in his village. The mantle of the old chief now fell on his brother Amar Singh who, despite heavy odds, continued the struggle and for a considerable time ran a parallel government in the then district of Shahabad. In October 1859 Amar Singh joined the rebel leaders in the Nepal Terai.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (A) कुँवर सिंह 1857 के सिपाही विद्रोह में सबसे महत्वपूर्ण स्वतंत्रता सेनानियों में से एक थे। कुँवर सिंह का जन्म बिहार के शाहाबाद (अब भोजपुर जिले में) के जगदीशपुर में हुआ था। गदर के दौरान वह बिहार के आरा के रहने वाले थे। 1857 में जब भारत के सभी भागों की जनता ब्रिटिश सत्ता के विरुद्ध उठ खड़ी हुई, तब बाबू कुँवर सिंह लगभग अस्सी वर्ष के थे। उस उम्र में उन्होंने अंग्रेजी ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी के खिलाफ लड़ाई लड़ी। अपनी उम्र और ख़राब स्वास्थ्य के बावजूद, कुँवर सिंह ने कड़ी मेहनत की और गंभीर दृढ़ संकल्प और अदम्य साहस के साथ ब्रिटिश सेना के खिलाफ लड़ाई लड़ी। बिहार में कुँवर सिंह अंग्रेजों के विरुद्ध नेता थे। उन्होंने 25 जुलाई 1857 को दानापुर में विद्रोह करने वाले सैनिकों की कमान संभाली। दो दिन बाद उन्होंने जिला मुख्यालय आरा पर कब्जा कर लिया। अगस्त 1857 में मेजर विंसेंट आयर ने शहर पर कब्ज़ा कर लिया, कुँवर सिंह की सेना को हरा दिया और जगदीशपुर को नष्ट कर दिया। दिसंबर 1857 में कुँवर सिंह अपना पैतृक गाँव छोड़कर लखनऊ पहुँचे। मार्च 1858 में उन्होंने आज़मगढ़ पर कब्ज़ा कर लिया। . हालाँकि, उन्हें जल्द ही वह जगह छोड़नी पड़ी। ब्रिगेडियर डगलस ने उनका पीछा किया और वह बिहार में अपने घर की ओर पीछे हट गए। 23 अप्रैल 1858 को, कुँवर सिंह ने कैप्टन ले ग्रैंड के नेतृत्व वाली सेना पर जगदीशपुर के पास जीत हासिल की, लेकिन 26 अप्रैल 1858 को उनके गाँव में उनकी मृत्यु हो गई। पुराने मुखिया का कार्यभार अब उनके भाई अमर सिंह पर आ गया, जिन्होंने भारी बाधाओं के बावजूद, संघर्ष जारी रखा और काफी समय तक शाहाबाद के तत्कालीन जिले में एक समानांतर सरकार चलाई। अक्टूबर 1859 में अमर सिंह नेपाल तराई में विद्रोही नेताओं में शामिल हो गये।

questions.questionTextEn: Who of the following was the bitterest enemy of the British during the Revolt of 1857?
questions.questionTextHi: 1857 के विद्रोह के दौरान निम्नलिखित में से कौन अंग्रेजों का सबसे कट्टर दुश्मन था?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). Maulavi Ahmadullah Shah was the bitterest enemy of Britishers. He led the 1857 revolt in Faizabad (Now Ayodhya). He was basically from Chinapattan (Madras), but later he resided in Faizabad (Now Ayodhya). The British considered him a worthy enemy and a great warrior in the following words “as a man of great abilities of undaunted courage, of stern determination and by far the best soldier among the rebels”. The British government announced a reward of Rs. 50000 for his arrest.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (A) मौलवी अहमदुल्ला शाह अंग्रेजों के कट्टर शत्रु थे। उन्होंने फैजाबाद (अब अयोध्या) में 1857 के विद्रोह का नेतृत्व किया। वह मूल रूप से चिनपट्टन (मद्रास) के रहने वाले थे, लेकिन बाद में वह फैजाबाद (अब अयोध्या) में रहने लगे। अंग्रेज़ उन्हें एक योग्य शत्रु और एक महान योद्धा मानते थे, इन शब्दों में कहें तो "निडर साहस, कठोर दृढ़ संकल्प और विद्रोहियों के बीच अब तक के सर्वश्रेष्ठ सैनिक की महान क्षमताओं वाला व्यक्ति"। ब्रिटिश सरकार ने रुपये के इनाम की घोषणा की। उसकी गिरफ्तारी के लिए 50000 रु.

questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). The revolt of 1857 was widespread and this rebellion had the popular support of the public. But it was suppressed to a greater extent. It was spread in limited areas. The entire South India, Punjab and the territory towards its north and west, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh remained out from the revolt. Many native rulers like the rulers of Patiala, Jind, Gwalior, Hyderabad, and the Sikhs of Punjab helped the British in suppressing the revolt by all possible means. The money lenders and merchants were also against the war as it was against their economic beneﬁ ts. The educated Indians and the middle class also did not support the revolt. On the contrary, their feelings were against it.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (D) 1857 का विद्रोह व्यापक था और इस विद्रोह को जनता का जनसमर्थन प्राप्त था। लेकिन इसे काफी हद तक दबा दिया गया. यह सीमित क्षेत्रों में फैला हुआ था। संपूर्ण दक्षिण भारत, पंजाब और उसके उत्तर और पश्चिम का क्षेत्र, राजस्थान, गुजरात और मध्य प्रदेश विद्रोह से बाहर रहे। कई देशी शासकों जैसे कि पटियाला, जिंद, ग्वालियर, हैदराबाद के शासकों और पंजाब के सिखों ने हर संभव तरीके से विद्रोह को दबाने में अंग्रेजों की मदद की। साहूकार और व्यापारी भी युद्ध के विरुद्ध थे क्योंकि यह उनके आर्थिक लाभ के विरुद्ध था। शिक्षित भारतीयों और मध्यम वर्ग ने भी विद्रोह का समर्थन नहीं किया। इसके विपरीत, उनकी भावनाएँ इसके विरुद्ध थीं।

questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा (1857 के विद्रोह का स्थान - विद्रोह की शुरुआत) सही सुमेलित नहीं है?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B). • On 29th March, 1857 soldiers of Barrackpore (West Bengal) refused to use the fat-containing cartridges and revolted. • On 10th May 1857, 3rd Bengal Light cavalry and twentieth regiment of British Indian Army positioned in Meerut revolted. • Revolt at Lucknow began on 30th May/4th June, 1857 under the leadership of Begum Hazrat Mahal. • Jhansi revolted on 4th June, 1857 under Rani Laxmi Bai. Note - In many reference books and oﬃ cial websites, the date of commencement of the Lucknow revolt of 1857 is given as 4th June, 1857, whereas in NCERT class 12 book, the date of beginning of this rebellion in Lucknow is given as 30 May 1857. questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). Lord Canning was Governer General of India during the 1857 revolt. Lord Canning was the last Governer General of the Company in India and the ﬁ rst Viceroy appointed by British Crown. Indian High Court Act 1861 introduced judicial reforms and established High Court in Bombay, Calcutta, and Madras during the tenure of Canning. questions.questionTextEn: Who was the prominent Indian Historian who did not accept 1857 Revolution as a Revolution?
questions.questionTextHi: वह प्रमुख भारतीय इतिहासकार कौन था जिसने 1857 की क्रांति को क्रांति के रूप में स्वीकार नहीं किया?
optionsEn: Dr. R.C. Majumdar (e) None of these
optionsHi: डॉ. आर.सी. मजूमदार (ई) इनमें से कोई नहीं
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). Indian Government appointed R.C. Majumdar to write the history of the revolt of 1857. But due to some diﬀ erences, he refused and published his own book ‘The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857’. Dr. R.C. Majumdar, however, considers the revolt of 1857 to be neither the ﬁ rst, nor national nor a war of independence as a large part of the country remained unaﬀ ected, and many sections of the people took no part in the upsurge.

questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following conceptions is true about the Revolt of 1857?
questions.questionTextHi: 1857 के विद्रोह के बारे में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी अवधारणा सत्य है?
optionsEn: Indian historians have described it as an Indian mutiny.
British historians have described it as a war of independence.
It gave a death blow to the system of East India Company’s rule in India
It was for the improvement of the administrative machinery in India
optionsHi: भारतीय इतिहासकारों ने इसे भारतीय विद्रोह बताया है।
ब्रिटिश इतिहासकारों ने इसे आज़ादी की लड़ाई बताया है।
इसने भारत में ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी के शासन की व्यवस्था को करारा झटका दिया
यह भारत में प्रशासनिक तंत्र में सुधार के लिए था
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). In the aftermath of 1857 revolt, East India company’s rule ended in India and the reign was handed over to Queen Victoria by a proclamation announced on November 1, 1858. She assumed the responsibility of the Indian administration in her hand. Hence, the option (c) is correct.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (C) 1857 के विद्रोह के बाद, भारत में ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी का शासन समाप्त हो गया और 1 नवंबर, 1858 को घोषित एक उद्घोषणा द्वारा शासन रानी विक्टोरिया को सौंप दिया गया। उन्होंने भारतीय प्रशासन की जिम्मेदारी अपने हाथ में ले ली। इसलिए, विकल्प (सी) सही है।

optionsEn: Policy of annexation will be abandoned
‘Status quo’ of the native rulers would be maintained
Equal treatment would be given to all subjects, Indians, and Europeans
There would be no interference in the social and religious beliefs of the Indians
optionsHi: विलय की नीति छोड़ दी जाएगी
सभी प्रजा, भारतीयों और यूरोपीय लोगों के साथ समान व्यवहार किया जाएगा

questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). The major result of 1857 revolt was the proclamation on November 1st, 1858 by Queen Victoria. This was proclaimed by Lord Canning during Allahabad Durbar. The ruthless, exploitative era of the East India Company was ended and a new era of British rule to be governed directly by British Crown began. This proclamation included the abandonment of the policy of conquest and annexation, adherence to the principles of secularism and religious neutrality and same judicial facilities to everyone without any discrimination. Among all these only abandonment of the policy of conquest and annexation was followed.

questions.questionTextHi: महारानी विक्टोरिया की उद्घोषणा (1858) का उद्देश्य क्या था/थे? 1. भारतीय राज्यों पर कब्ज़ा करने के किसी भी इरादे को अस्वीकार करना 2. भारतीय प्रशासन को ब्रिटिश क्राउन के अधीन रखना 3. भारत के साथ ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी के व्यापार को विनियमित करना नीचे दिए गए कोड का उपयोग करके सही उत्तर चुनें।
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). British Government passed an Act in 1858, which is known as ‘Act of administrative reforms in India’. Provision of the Act is mentioned below – The company’s territories in India were to be governed by Queen, the company ceased to exercise its power and control over these territories. India was now to be governed in the name of the queen. The Queen’s principal secretary of state for India received the powers and duties of the company’s court of directors. A council of ﬁ fteen members was appointed to assist the secretary of state for India. The Council became an advisory body of Indian aﬀ airs. For all the communications between Britain and India, the secretary of the state became the real channel. The Crown was empowered to appoint a Governor-General and the Governors of the Presidencies. An Indian Civil Service was to be created under the control of the secretary of state. All the property and other assets of the East India Company were transferred to the crown. The crown also assumed the responsibilities of the company, their related treaties, contracts and so forth.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (A) ब्रिटिश सरकार ने 1858 में एक अधिनियम पारित किया, जिसे 'भारत में प्रशासनिक सुधार अधिनियम' के नाम से जाना जाता है। अधिनियम के प्रावधान नीचे उल्लिखित हैं - भारत में कंपनी के क्षेत्र रानी द्वारा शासित होने थे, कंपनी ने इन क्षेत्रों पर अपनी शक्ति का प्रयोग और नियंत्रण बंद कर दिया। अब भारत का शासन रानी के नाम पर किया जाना था। भारत के लिए महारानी के प्रधान सचिव को कंपनी के निदेशक मंडल की शक्तियाँ और कर्तव्य प्राप्त हुए। भारत के राज्य सचिव की सहायता के लिए पंद्रह सदस्यों की एक परिषद नियुक्त की गई। परिषद भारतीय वायुसेना की एक सलाहकार संस्था बन गई। ब्रिटेन और भारत के बीच सभी संचारों के लिए राज्य सचिव ही वास्तविक माध्यम बन गया। क्राउन को गवर्नर-जनरल और प्रेसीडेंसी के गवर्नर नियुक्त करने का अधिकार दिया गया था। राज्य सचिव के नियंत्रण में एक भारतीय सिविल सेवा बनाई जानी थी। ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी की सारी संपत्ति और अन्य परिसंपत्तियाँ ताज को हस्तांतरित कर दी गईं। क्राउन ने कंपनी की ज़िम्मेदारियाँ, उनकी संबंधित संधियाँ, अनुबंध आदि भी संभाले।
